traditions.name: The Pentecostal Mission (Ceylon Pentecostal Mission)
traditions.summary: Founded in Colombo, Ceylon, in 1923 by Pastor Paul (born Ramankutty, a Keralite convert from Hinduism) with Alwin R. de Alwis, and known first as the Ceylon Pentecostal Mission. Its international headquarters is now at Irumbuliyur near Tambaram, Chennai. It is an indigenous South Asian Pentecostal church best known for its celibate, propertyless ministers who live in communal 'faith homes' and dress entirely in white.
distinctives: Full-time ministers, men and women, are celibate, hold no private property and live together in faith homes
Ministers and worshippers wear white; jewellery and ornaments are renounced
Strong emphasis on divine healing, with ministers declining medical treatment
Teaching that sanctified 'overcomers' will form the company of Mount Zion (Revelation 14)
Large annual conventions, including the international convention in Chennai
Congregations known in different countries as CPM, TPM, Zion Pentecostal Mission or New Testament Church

profile.authority: Scripture, read in a holiness-Pentecostal way, with great weight on the instruction of the senior ministers.
profile.salvation: Salvation by grace through repentance and faith, followed by water baptism, sanctification and Baptism in the Holy Spirit evidenced by tongues; a life of separation from the world is stressed.
profile.sacraments: Baptism of believers by immersion and the Lord's Supper; footwashing is practised in some settings.
profile.eschatology: Premillennial; the faithful and sanctified are taught to await the rapture and a place with Christ in Zion.
profile.governance: A centralised ministry under a chief pastor and senior ministers; local faith homes direct the congregations.
profile.worship: Simple Pentecostal services with congregational singing, testimony and prayer; worshippers sit on the floor and dress in white.

traditions.status: Active in India, Sri Lanka and among South Asian diaspora communities worldwide.

traditions.name: Believers Eastern Church
traditions.summary: An episcopal church that grew out of the Gospel for Asia (now GFA World) mission founded by K. P. Yohannan of Niranam, Kerala, in 1979. Organised as Believers Church in 1993, it adopted episcopal government in 2003 with Yohannan as first Metropolitan, and took the name Believers Eastern Church in 2017 to express affinity with the ancient Eastern churches. Headquartered in Thiruvalla, Kerala, it combines evangelical teaching with Eastern-style vestments, liturgy and titles. After Yohannan's death in 2024, Samuel Mor Theophilus was elected Metropolitan.
distinctives: Evangelical doctrine within an Eastern-style episcopal and liturgical form
Grew from the Gospel for Asia mission's support of native missionaries
Strong rural mission work across North India, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Myanmar
Runs Believers Church Medical College Hospital and schools in Thiruvalla
Has faced public scrutiny over GFA finances in the United States and India

profile.authority: Scripture as the final authority, received within what the church calls the ancient apostolic and Eastern tradition.
profile.salvation: Salvation by grace through personal faith in Christ, with a strong call to evangelism.
profile.sacraments: Baptism and the Holy Qurbana (Eucharist) celebrated with an Eastern-style liturgy.
profile.eschatology: Expectation of Christ's return; not a central point of controversy.
profile.governance: Episcopal: a Metropolitan and bishops with a synod, organised into dioceses.
profile.worship: Liturgical worship in Malayalam, Hindi and other languages, with vestments and Eastern titles.

traditions.status: Active; dioceses in India and neighbouring countries.

traditions.name: St. Thomas Evangelical Church of India
traditions.summary: An evangelical episcopal church in Kerala that separated from the Mar Thoma Syrian Church on 26 January 1961, after a long dispute and lawsuit in which lay leader K. N. Daniel accused the Mar Thoma leadership of drifting back towards Jacobite (Syriac Orthodox) doctrine and practice. The courts ruled against Daniel, the Supreme Court giving final judgement in 1965. Headquartered at Manjadi, Thiruvalla, it keeps a reformed Malankara heritage with a stronger evangelical emphasis.
distinctives: Separated from the Mar Thoma Church in 1961 over the purity of its reformation
Episcopal government with a presiding bishop
Evangelical preaching, revival conventions and missionary work
Shares the Malayalam reformed-Syrian heritage of the Mar Thoma Church

profile.authority: Scripture as the sole rule of faith, as the Mar Thoma reformers of the nineteenth century had urged.
profile.salvation: Salvation by grace through faith in Christ; personal conversion and assurance are emphasised.
profile.sacraments: Baptism and the Lord's Supper as the two sacraments of the Gospel.
profile.governance: Episcopal, with bishops, clergy and an elected representative assembly.
profile.worship: Malayalam liturgy derived from the reformed Mar Thoma order, with evangelical hymnody and preaching.

traditions.status: Active, mainly in Kerala and the Malayali diaspora.

traditions.name: Tamil Evangelical Lutheran Church
traditions.summary: The church of Tamil Nadu that descends from the first Protestant mission in India, begun at Tranquebar (Tharangambadi) in 1706 by Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg and Heinrich Plütschau of the Danish-Halle Mission, and later continued by the Leipzig Mission. It was constituted as an autonomous church in 1919, with headquarters at Tiruchirappalli; its first Indian bishop, Rajah B. Manikam, was consecrated in 1956.
distinctives: Heir of Ziegenbalg's Tranquebar mission, the first Protestant mission in India (1706)
Episcopal Lutheran church holding the Augsburg Confession and Luther's Small Catechism
Tamil Bible and hymn tradition reaching back to Ziegenbalg and Vedanayagam Sastri
Schools, hospitals and the Gurukul Lutheran Theological College tradition

profile.authority: Scripture as the norm, with the Lutheran Confessions as its faithful exposition.
profile.salvation: Justification by grace through faith alone, for Christ's sake.
profile.sacraments: Baptism (including infants) and the Lord's Supper, in which Christ's body and blood are truly present.
profile.eschatology: Christ's return to judge the living and the dead.
profile.governance: Episcopal: a bishop with a church council and synod, headquartered in Tiruchirappalli.
profile.worship: Lutheran liturgy in Tamil with Tamil lyrics (keerthanai) alongside translated chorales.

traditions.status: Active; a member of the Lutheran World Federation and the United Evangelical Lutheran Churches in India.

traditions.name: Andhra Evangelical Lutheran Church
traditions.summary: The largest Lutheran church in India, based in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh. It grew from the mission begun on 31 July 1842 by John Christian Frederick ('Father') Heyer of the Lutheran General Synod in America, and was constituted as a self-governing church in 1927. Its growth came largely through Dalit (Mala and Madiga) mass movements in the coastal Andhra delta.
distinctives: Founded on Father Heyer's 1842 mission in Guntur
Largest Lutheran church in India, with Telugu-speaking membership
Grew through Dalit group conversions in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries
Andhra Christian College, hospitals and schools in Guntur and Rajahmundry

profile.sacraments: Infant baptism and the Lord's Supper with real presence.
profile.eschatology: Return of Christ and final judgement.
profile.governance: Episcopal: a bishop with a church council, synods and districts.

traditions.status: Active; member of the Lutheran World Federation.

traditions.name: Indian Brethren (Kerala Brethren assemblies)
traditions.summary: Autonomous Open Brethren assemblies in India. Anthony Norris Groves brought Brethren principles to India from 1833, and his disciple John Arulappan spread them among Tamils; in Kerala the movement is dated to March 1899, when four men broke bread without a priest at Kumbanad after the preaching of the English evangelist J. G. Gregson. The German missionary Volbrecht Nagel, formerly of the Basel Mission, became its leading pioneer, and many early members came from Mar Thoma and other Syrian Christian families.
distinctives: No ordained clergy; weekly 'breaking of bread' led by the brothers
Each assembly autonomous, with no central governing body
Believer's baptism by immersion and strong lay preaching
Large gospel conventions, notably at Kumbanad
Women veil their heads and do not speak in the assembly meeting

profile.authority: Scripture alone, read with a literal and dispensational hermeneutic.
profile.salvation: Salvation by grace through faith; assurance of salvation stressed.
profile.sacraments: Believer's baptism by immersion and the weekly Lord's Supper as a memorial.
profile.eschatology: Dispensational premillennialism with a pre-tribulation rapture.
profile.governance: Congregational: each assembly led by recognised elders.
profile.worship: Unstructured worship meetings with open participation by men; Malayalam hymnody (e.g. K. V. Simon).

traditions.status: Active in Kerala, other Indian states and the Gulf and Western diaspora.

traditions.name: Sharon Fellowship Church
traditions.summary: An indigenous Pentecostal church founded in 1953 at Thiruvalla, Kerala, by Pastor P. J. Thomas (1914–1998), who had studied at Serampore and Wheaton College, together with T. G. Koshy and ten others. It grew from the Sharon Bible School on property Thomas bought in March 1953 and is known for combining Pentecostal piety with an emphasis on theological education.
distinctives: Indigenous Kerala Pentecostal church with Indian leadership from the start
Emphasis on trained ministry through Sharon Bible College
Linked with the founding of Faith Theological Seminary, Manakala
Classical Pentecostal theology with relatively moderate dress rules

profile.salvation: Salvation by grace through faith; Spirit baptism with speaking in tongues as a subsequent experience.
profile.sacraments: Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper.
profile.governance: General council with regional centres and local pastors.
profile.worship: Pentecostal worship in Malayalam and other languages.

traditions.status: Active in Kerala, other Indian states and the diaspora.

traditions.name: Church of God (Full Gospel) in India
traditions.summary: The Indian branch of the Church of God (Cleveland, Tennessee), headquartered at Mulakuzha near Chengannur, Kerala. It began with the American missionary Robert F. Cook, who reached India in 1913, moved his work to Kerala and by 1923 had founded some 36 congregations; his work joined the Church of God in 1936. K. E. Abraham, once Cook's associate, left in 1930 to found what became the Indian Pentecostal Church of God.
distinctives: Indian arm of the Church of God (Cleveland)
Headquarters at Mulakuzha, Kerala
Separate structures for Kerala and other regions
Strong among Dalit Christians of central Travancore

profile.authority: Scripture with the Church of God Declaration of Faith.
profile.salvation: Justification, sanctification and Spirit baptism evidenced by tongues.
profile.sacraments: Baptism by immersion, Lord's Supper and footwashing.
profile.governance: Episcopal-style overseers appointed within the Church of God structure.
profile.worship: Pentecostal worship in Malayalam and other languages.

traditions.name: Assemblies of God in India
traditions.summary: The Indian fellowship of the Assemblies of God, rooted in missionary work from 1915–16 and formally organised in 1918, with Christian H. Schoonmaker as founding chairman. Bethel Bible College in Punalur, Kerala (1927), was the first permanent Assemblies of God Bible school outside the United States. Its General Council, headquartered in Chennai, was formed in 1995 and joins regional councils such as the South India Assemblies of God.
distinctives: Indian member of the World Assemblies of God Fellowship
Bethel Bible College, Punalur (1927)
Regional district councils for Kerala, Tamil Nadu and North India
Large urban congregations such as New Life Assembly of God, Chennai

profile.authority: Scripture with the Assemblies of God Statement of Fundamental Truths.
profile.salvation: Salvation by grace through faith; Spirit baptism evidenced by tongues.
profile.sacraments: Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper as ordinances.
profile.governance: Cooperative fellowship: autonomous churches in district councils under a General Council.
profile.worship: Contemporary and traditional Pentecostal worship in many languages.

traditions.name: Apostolic Christian Assembly
traditions.summary: An indigenous Pentecostal church of Chennai that began in 1948 as a home Bible study led by Pastor G. Sundaram and his wife Beatrice in Purasawalkam. After G. Sundaram's death in 1989, his son M. K. Sam Sundaram became chief pastor and led its growth into one of the best-known Tamil Pentecostal churches; on his death in 2015 he was succeeded by Caleb Joshua. Branches such as Avadi (1973) and K. K. Nagar spread across the city.
distinctives: Tamil indigenous Pentecostal church with family-led leadership
Mother church at Purasawalkam, Chennai, with daughter congregations
Emphasis on prayer, fasting and healing
Tamil-language worship and preaching

profile.salvation: Salvation by grace through faith; Spirit baptism with tongues.
profile.sacraments: Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper.
profile.governance: A chief pastor leading a network of branch churches.
profile.worship: Tamil Pentecostal worship with prayer and testimony.

traditions.name: Presbyterian Church of India
traditions.summary: The largest Protestant church of North-East India, headquartered in Shillong. It began when Thomas Jones of the Welsh Calvinistic Methodist mission reached Sohra (Cherrapunji) on 22 June 1841, and spread through the Khasi-Jaintia and Lushai (Mizo) hills to Cachar, Manipur and Tripura. A Synod was formed in 1926; in 1953 this became the General Assembly, with the regional assemblies renamed synods, among which the Mizoram Synod is the largest.
distinctives: Heir of the Welsh Calvinistic Methodist mission to the Khasi and Mizo peoples
Khasi and Mizo written languages first put into Roman script by missionaries
Shaped by revivals, notably the Khasi revival of 1905 and repeated Mizo revivals
Synods with strong self-support and mission programmes

profile.authority: Scripture, with the church's confession of faith in the Reformed tradition.
profile.salvation: Salvation by grace through faith in Christ.
profile.sacraments: Baptism (including infants) and the Lord's Supper.
profile.eschatology: Return of Christ and final judgement.
profile.governance: Presbyterian: presbyteries, synods and a General Assembly.
profile.worship: Reformed worship with strong congregational singing in Khasi, Mizo and other languages.

traditions.status: Active; member of the Council for World Mission and the World Communion of Reformed Churches.

traditions.name: Council of Baptist Churches in North East India
traditions.summary: A council of Baptist conventions in North-East India, headquartered in Guwahati. American Baptist missionaries reached Assam in 1836; in January 1950 their work became the Council of Baptist Churches in Assam, later renamed for the whole North-East. Its member conventions serve Assamese, Garo, Naga, Mizo, Karbi, Kuki and other communities.
distinctives: Umbrella body for many tribal Baptist conventions
Heir of the American Baptist mission begun in 1836
Serves the Garo Baptist Convention and others
Theological training at Eastern Theological College, Jorhat

profile.sacraments: Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper.
profile.governance: Congregational churches in associations and conventions.
profile.worship: Evangelical worship in many local languages.

traditions.status: Active; member of the Baptist World Alliance.

traditions.name: Nagaland Baptist Church Council
traditions.summary: The council of Baptist churches in Nagaland, headquartered in Kohima. American Baptist work among the Ao Nagas began in the 1870s through the Assamese evangelist Godhula and missionary E. W. Clark; a council of churches was formed in 1937 as the Naga Hills Baptist Church Council. Today it links tribal associations (Ao, Angami, Lotha, Sumi and others) in one of India's few Baptist-majority states.
distinctives: Represents a Baptist-majority population in Nagaland
Tribal associations under one council
Revival movements in the 1950s and 1970s
Advocacy for alcohol prohibition and for peace in the Naga conflict

profile.sacraments: Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper.
profile.worship: Evangelical worship with strong choral singing.

traditions.status: Active; member of the Baptist World Alliance through its member bodies.

traditions.name: Evangelical Church of India
traditions.summary: An episcopal evangelical church headquartered in Chennai, which arose from the work of the Oriental Missionary Society (now One Mission Society) and opened its first church in 1954. Under M. Ezra Sargunam (d. 2024), its first bishop, it grew through urban church planting among Tamils and others, reaching his target of 1,000 churches by 1997. It runs the Madras Theological Seminary and College.
distinctives: Indigenous episcopal church from the OMS holiness tradition
Rapid church planting under Ezra Sargunam
Madras Theological Seminary and College
Social advocacy for Dalit Christians

profile.salvation: Salvation by grace through faith and holiness of life.
profile.worship: Evangelical liturgy in Tamil and other languages.

traditions.name: New Life Fellowship (India)
traditions.summary: A charismatic church network begun in Pune in 1964 by New Zealand missionaries Graham and Pamela Truscott of the New Life Churches. Established in Mumbai in 1966, it grew under S. Joseph through many small house-based congregations.
distinctives: Many small, house-based congregations
Charismatic worship
Lay leadership
Strong presence in Mumbai

profile.salvation: Salvation by grace through faith; Spirit baptism.
profile.sacraments: Believer's baptism and the Lord's Supper.
profile.governance: Network of local churches with central leadership.

traditions.name: Myanmar Baptist Convention
traditions.summary: The largest Protestant body in Myanmar, formed in 1865 as the Burma Baptist Missionary Convention. It descends from the mission of Adoniram and Ann Hasseltine Judson, who arrived in Rangoon in 1813. Most members belong to ethnic minorities such as Karen, Kachin and Chin.
distinctives: Heir of the Judson mission
Mainly ethnic-minority membership
Judson's Burmese Bible (1834)
Witness amid civil conflict

profile.sacraments: Believer's baptism and the Lord's Supper.

traditions.name: Church of Christ in Thailand
traditions.summary: Thailand's largest Protestant body, formed in 1934 mainly from the American Presbyterian mission (Bangkok from 1840; Chiang Mai from 1867 under Daniel McGilvary).
distinctives: Mainly Presbyterian roots
Strong in northern Thailand
Hospitals and schools such as Payap University

traditions.name: Protestant Church in Indonesia (Gereja Protestan di Indonesia)
traditions.summary: The successor of the Dutch colonial state church (the Indische Kerk), whose roots go back to the first Protestant services in Ambon in 1605. It is now a federation of twelve autonomous churches, including GMIM, GPM, GMIT and GPIB.
distinctives: Successor of the colonial state church
Federation of regional churches
Strong in Maluku, Minahasa and Timor

profile.sacraments: Infant baptism and the Lord's Supper.

traditions.name: Methodist Church Sri Lanka
traditions.summary: Wesleyan missionaries sent with Thomas Coke (who died at sea in 1814) landed at Galle in 1814; the church became an autonomous conference in 1964.
distinctives: One of the oldest Methodist churches in Asia
Autonomous since 1964
Sinhala, Tamil and English work

denomProfiles.tagline: White-clad, celibate ministers in faith homes: South Asia's distinctive holiness Pentecostal church.
coreDoctrines: Trinitarian Pentecostal faith with Spirit baptism evidenced by tongues
Entire sanctification and separation from worldly display
Divine healing as the believer's provision, without reliance on medicine
An elect 'Zion' company of overcomers who follow the Lamb (Revelation 14:1–5)
focuses: Holiness of life and simplicity of dress
Faith living: ministers receive no salary and solicit no funds
Evangelism through conventions and faith homes
practices: Ministers renounce marriage and possessions and live communally
White clothing for ministers and members at worship; no jewellery

influencedBy.name: Pentecostalism
influencedBy.text: The Azusa Street revival's message of Spirit baptism reached Ceylon and Kerala through early Pentecostal missionaries.

influencedBy.name: Holiness Movement
influencedBy.text: Its teaching on entire sanctification and separation shaped the mission's strict holiness ethic.

influencedBy.name: Indian ascetic ideals
influencedBy.text: The renunciant life of the ministers echoes the South Asian ideal of the sannyasi.

influenced.name: South Indian Pentecostalism
influenced.text: Its strict holiness ethos, white dress and plain living shaped expectations across Kerala and Tamil Pentecostal churches.

influenced.name: Diaspora congregations
influenced.text: Tamil, Malayali and Sinhala migrants planted TPM congregations across the Gulf, Europe, North America and Malaysia.

keyFigures.name: Pastor Paul (Ramankutty)
keyFigures.role: Founder (d. 1945), a Keralite convert from Hinduism

keyFigures.name: Alwin R. de Alwis
keyFigures.role: Co-founder in Colombo; later separated from the mission

denomProfiles.inIndia: Headquartered at Irumbuliyur, Chennai, it is strong in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, where its white-clad ministers and large conventions are a familiar sight; Bergunder treats it as one of the most distinctive indigenous South Indian Pentecostal bodies.

denomProfiles.tagline: Evangelical mission church from Kerala that adopted Eastern episcopacy and liturgy.
coreDoctrines: Nicene Trinitarian faith and evangelical conversion
Episcopacy in continuity with ancient churches
focuses: Rural church planting in North India

influencedBy.name: Gospel for Asia
influencedBy.text: The mission K. P. Yohannan founded in 1979 provided the church's workers and funding base.

influencedBy.name: Saint Thomas Christian tradition
influencedBy.text: Its Kerala setting shaped the turn to Eastern liturgy and episcopacy.

influencedBy.name: Evangelicalism
influencedBy.text: Yohannan's conversion and training with Operation Mobilisation gave the church its evangelical theology.

influenced.name: Indigenous missions movement
influenced.text: Its native-missionary model was widely copied by Western support agencies.

denomProfiles.inIndia: Headquartered in Thiruvalla, Kerala, with dioceses across North and South India; its medical college hospital is a major institution in central Travancore.

denomProfiles.tagline: Kerala's evangelical offshoot of the Mar Thoma Church, formed in 1961.
focuses: Guarding against what it sees as a return to pre-reform rites

influencedBy.name: Mar Thoma Syrian Church
influencedBy.text: Its parent church, from which it took its liturgy and polity.

influencedBy.name: Church Missionary Society
influencedBy.text: CMS evangelical teaching behind the nineteenth-century Mar Thoma reform shaped its theology.

influencedBy.name: Abraham Malpan
influencedBy.text: The reformer of the 1830s whose programme the church claims to carry on.

keyFigures.name: K. N. Daniel
keyFigures.role: Lay leader whose lawsuit preceded the separation

denomProfiles.inIndia: Centred on Manjadi, Thiruvalla, in Kerala, with congregations among Malayalis elsewhere in India; Wikipedia gives over 350 congregations.

denomProfiles.tagline: Tamil Nadu's Lutheran church, rooted in Ziegenbalg's 1706 Tranquebar mission.
coreDoctrines: The Augsburg Confession and Small Catechism
Real presence in the Lord's Supper
focuses: Social service through schools and hospitals

influencedBy.name: Danish-Halle Mission
influencedBy.text: Ziegenbalg and Plütschau founded the first Protestant church in India at Tranquebar.

influencedBy.name: Leipzig Mission
influencedBy.text: Took over the Tamil Lutheran field from 1840 and guided it to autonomy.

influencedBy.name: Vedanayagam Sastri
influencedBy.text: Tamil poet of Thanjavur whose hymns gave the church an indigenous voice.

influenced.name: Church of South India
influenced.text: Tamil Protestant traditions from the Tranquebar mission fed into the wider Tamil church, including congregations later in the CSI.

influenced.name: Tamil Bible translation
influenced.text: Ziegenbalg's New Testament of 1714 began the Tamil Protestant Bible tradition.

denomProfiles.inIndia: Based in Tiruchirappalli and strongest in the Thanjavur, Tranquebar and Cuddalore districts of Tamil Nadu; it is one of the oldest Protestant churches in Asia.

denomProfiles.tagline: India's largest Lutheran church, born from Father Heyer's 1842 mission in Guntur.

influencedBy.name: American Lutheran mission
influencedBy.text: Heyer and the General Synod mission (later the United Lutheran Church in America) founded the work.

influencedBy.name: Dalit mass movements
influencedBy.text: Group conversions in coastal Andhra shaped the church's social make-up and concerns.

influenced.name: United Evangelical Lutheran Churches in India
influenced.text: As the largest member it has weighed heavily in Indian Lutheran cooperation.

denomProfiles.inIndia: Concentrated in Guntur, Krishna, Godavari and Prakasam districts of Andhra Pradesh; it reports membership in the millions, though published figures vary widely.

denomProfiles.tagline: Clergy-free Brethren assemblies, strong in Kerala since the 1899 Kumbanad meeting.
coreDoctrines: Priesthood of all believers without ordained clergy
focuses: Mission in North India through workers 'commended' by assemblies

influencedBy.name: Open Brethren
influencedBy.text: The British movement whose principles Groves and later evangelists carried to India.

influencedBy.name: Anthony Norris Groves
influencedBy.text: His faith-mission model in India from 1833 seeded Brethren ideas among Indians.

influencedBy.name: Mar Thoma Syrian Church
influencedBy.text: Many early Kerala Brethren came from reformed Syrian Christian families.

influenced.name: Kerala Pentecostalism
influenced.text: Several early Kerala Pentecostal leaders came out of Brethren assemblies and kept their Bible-study style.

influenced.name: Indigenous Indian missions
influenced.text: Brethren-commended workers planted churches across North India.

keyFigures.name: Volbrecht Nagel
keyFigures.role: German missionary and pioneer of Kerala assemblies

keyFigures.name: K. V. Simon
keyFigures.role: Malayalam hymn writer and early leader

denomProfiles.inIndia: Strongest in central Kerala (Kumbanad, Thiruvalla, Kottayam) and coastal Andhra; Kerala Brethren have sent many workers to North India and the Gulf.

denomProfiles.tagline: Thiruvalla Pentecostal church founded by P. J. Thomas, known for theological training.
focuses: Evangelism in Kerala and North India

influencedBy.name: Pentecostalism
influencedBy.text: Classical Pentecostal teaching on Spirit baptism.

influencedBy.name: Evangelical theological education
influencedBy.text: Thomas's studies at Serampore and Wheaton shaped the church's stress on training.

influenced.name: Faith Theological Seminary
influenced.text: Founded by T. G. Koshy, a co-founder of Sharon, it trained many Kerala evangelical leaders.

keyFigures.name: T. G. Koshy
keyFigures.role: Co-founder; later founder of Faith Theological Seminary

denomProfiles.inIndia: Headquartered in Thiruvalla, Kerala, with congregations across India and among Malayalis abroad.

denomProfiles.tagline: Kerala-based Indian branch of the Church of God (Cleveland), founded by Robert F. Cook.
coreDoctrines: Church of God Declaration of Faith

influencedBy.name: Church of God (Cleveland)
influencedBy.text: Its parent body supplies doctrine and polity.

influencedBy.name: Robert F. Cook
influencedBy.text: American missionary who built the Kerala work from 1913.

influenced.name: Indian Pentecostal Church of God
influenced.text: K. E. Abraham's break with Cook in 1930 led to India's largest indigenous Pentecostal church.

denomProfiles.inIndia: Centred at Mulakuzha in Kerala, with regional organisations in Tamil Nadu and other states.

denomProfiles.tagline: Indian Assemblies of God, from Punalur's Bethel Bible College to Chennai's megachurches.
coreDoctrines: Spirit baptism with initial evidence of tongues

influencedBy.name: Assemblies of God
influencedBy.text: American missionaries founded and long supported the work.

influenced.name: Indian urban Pentecostalism
influenced.text: Its large city churches set patterns for independent charismatic congregations.

denomProfiles.inIndia: Present across India; strongest in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, with its General Council headquartered in Chennai.

denomProfiles.tagline: Chennai Pentecostal church begun in 1948 by G. Sundaram, led later by Sam Sundaram.

influencedBy.name: Pentecostalism
influencedBy.text: Classical Pentecostal teaching formed its doctrine.

denomProfiles.inIndia: Based in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, with branches across the city and beyond.

denomProfiles.tagline: Welsh-rooted Presbyterian church of the Khasi and Mizo hills, centred in Shillong.
coreDoctrines: Spiritual presence in the Lord's Supper
focuses: Self-supporting mission to other states and abroad

influencedBy.name: Welsh Calvinistic Methodism
influencedBy.text: The mission of the Presbyterian Church of Wales founded and shaped the church.

influencedBy.name: Welsh revival of 1904–05
influencedBy.text: Its spirit spread to the Khasi Hills in 1905.

influenced.name: Christianity in Mizoram
influenced.text: Mizoram became one of India's majority-Christian states.

denomProfiles.inIndia: Strongest in Meghalaya and Mizoram, with synods in Manipur, Assam and elsewhere in the North-East.

denomProfiles.tagline: Guwahati-based council of tribal Baptist conventions in North-East India.

influencedBy.name: American Baptist Foreign Mission Society
influencedBy.text: Its missionaries founded the work from 1836.

influenced.name: Nagaland Baptist Church Council
influenced.text: One of its key member conventions.

denomProfiles.inIndia: Across North-East India, especially Assam, Nagaland, Manipur, Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh.

denomProfiles.tagline: Kohima-based council uniting the Baptist churches of Nagaland.

influencedBy.name: American Baptist mission
influencedBy.text: Clark and Godhula's work among the Ao Nagas.

influenced.name: Naga missionary movement
influenced.text: It sends missionaries to other parts of India and Asia.

keyFigures.name: E. W. Clark
keyFigures.role: American Baptist missionary among the Ao Nagas

denomProfiles.inIndia: Concentrated in Nagaland, where most of the population is Baptist.
